limitations: Timings are exploratory, not a verified production speedup. Background applications remained active and substantial load changes were observed, particularly during output-neuron tests.

Cache sizing has one observation per configuration/position; the last match/four-ply cases overlapped an experimental compilation. Use it to reject a blanket memory increase, not to claim precise speedups.
The 300-position pass checks numerical parity at fixed 2-ply settings; it does not measure stronger play or phone performance.
Original per-run metadata/hashes are preserved. This summary additionally hashes complete numerical outputs; rounded timing display is not used for assertions.

profile.method: One diagnostic first search with Chromium CPU sampling at 1000 µs, named -g2 build, normal optimization flags. Function self-time includes inlined code. Profiler overhead and background activity affect durations; percentages describe this position only.

experiments.method: Cache-size diagnostic; no search/weight/filter changes. Fresh worker/native caches per sample, local HTTP, startup excluded, configuration order rotated across repetitions. Browser compilation/HTTP caches may be warm. Not phone measurements. Allocation is before timing; heap size includes allocator growth/fragmentation.

Paired first-search native comparison. Fresh worker/native caches per sample; alternating baseline/candidate order; startup recorded separately; local HTTP and warm browser compilation/HTTP caches possible. Identical JS evaluator, canonical states, weights, presets and candidate filters. Not real-phone measurements. No concurrent heavy local test jobs.
